merger_name: Estia Health – AnglicareSA residential aged care business
merger_description:
Estia Investments Pty Ltd (**Estia**) proposes to acquire substantially all the business assets of six residential aged care homes from Anglicare SA Ltd (**AnglicareSA**):

* AnglicareSA Grange
* AnglicareSA Trott Park
* AnglicareSA Elizabeth East
* AnglicareSA Brompton
* AnglicareSA Elizabeth – Dutton Court, and
* AnglicareSA Westbourne Park

(**Proposed Acquisition**).

Estia is a registered provider of residential care services. Estia and its wholly owned subsidiaries currently operate over 90 residential aged care homes across Victoria, New South Wales, Queensland, and South Australia. Estia is currently majority owned by Bain Capital Private Equity. On 22 July 2026, the ACCC determined under section 51ABZE(1) that the acquisition of Estia by a Stonepeak-led consortium may be put into effect, see https://www.accc.gov.au/public-registers/mergers-and-acquisitions-registers/acquisitions-register/stonepeak-led-consortium-estia-health.

AnglicareSA is an independent not-for-profit organisation and a registered provider of care services. It operates six residential aged care homes in Adelaide (being the homes Estia Health proposes to acquire). AnglicareSA also provides other services to the community, including community aged care, NDIS services, foster care, mental health, financial counselling, community housing and support for vulnerable individuals. AnglicareSA intends to continue providing these other services following the Proposed Acquisition.

Estia and AnglicareSA both operate residential aged care homes in certain areas within, and in the outer suburbs of, metropolitan Adelaide.

events.title: Estia Health-AnglicareSA residential aged care business - Phase 1 determination
events.determination_commission_division: Determination made by a division of the Commission constituted by a direction issued pursuant to section 19 of the Act

determination_table_content.details:
Estia Investments Pty Ltd (Estia)’s proposed acquisition of
substantially all the business assets of six residential aged care
homes from Anglicare SA Ltd (AnglicareSA):
• AnglicareSA Grange
• AnglicareSA Trott Park
• AnglicareSA Elizabeth East
• AnglicareSA Brompton
• AnglicareSA Elizabeth – Dutton Court, and
• AnglicareSA Westbourne Park
(the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, Estia, is a registered provider of residential care
services. Estia and its wholly owned subsidiaries currently operate
over 90 residential aged care homes across Victoria, New South
Wales, Queensland, and South Australia.
Estia is currently majority owned by Bain Capital Private
Equity. However, on 22 July 2026, the ACCC determined under
section 51ABZE(1) that the acquisition of Estia by a Stonepeak-led
consortium may be put into effect, see ACCC determination.
AnglicareSA is an independent not-for-profit organisation and a
registered provider of care services. It operates six residential aged
care homes in Adelaide (being the homes Estia Health proposes to
acquire). AnglicareSA also provides other services to the
community, including community aged care, NDIS services, foster
care, mental health, financial counselling, community housing and
support for vulnerable individuals. AnglicareSA intends to continue
providing these other services following the Acquisition.

Estia and AnglicareSA (together, the Parties) overlap in the supply of
residential aged care homes in certain areas within, and in the outer
suburbs of, metropolitan Adelaide.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, information from third partes, and publicly
available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The aggregation arising from the Acquisition, and taking into
account previous acquisitions by Estia within the same local
area as the AnglicareSA facilities in the last three years, is not
significant at a local or regional level (nor at the national level).
• Estia would likely continue to face competition from alternative
suppliers of residential aged care facilities in the local areas
surrounding each of the AnglicareSA facilities. This includes
competition from alternative residential aged care facilities
located close to each of the AnglicareSA facilities, which the
ACCC considered to be close competitors to the AnglicareSA
facilities.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.
